report.summary: Chunk 1 of 6: module docstring, constants, and public symbol exports. No executable code; all claims are about design, measurements, and invariants. Most claims are uncheckable because they refer to external measurements or code not present.
risks: WHY_READ_ATTRIBUTES | medium | Claim about os.fstat(1) behavior with strict mask is uncheckable; if wrong, gate may still be blind.
UNMEASURED entry 'named pipes' | medium | Claim that named pipes were not measured is stated, but if a test later claims coverage, this is a risk.
JOB_ACTIVE_PROCESS_LIMIT | low | Claim that limit is based on measured peak with margin; no measurement code in chunk.
JOB_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES | low | Claim of 4 GiB limit, but no enforcement code present.
LOW_APPEND_ACCESS mask | high | Claim that mask equals 0x00100084 is checked by code; if wrong, containment broken. Verdict: kept.
UNMEASURED tuple | medium | Claim that test fails if original entries disappear; no test code present.
todos: Verify that WHY_READ_ATTRIBUTES measurement is documented elsewhere.
Ensure that UNMEASURED tuple is actually enforced by a test.
Check that JOB_ACTIVE_PROCESS_LIMIT and JOB_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES are used in job creation code.
Confirm that LOW_APPEND_ACCESS mask is used consistently in NtCreateFile calls.

claims.text: A child launched at Low integrity, with the worktree labelled Low: REFUSED BY THE KERNEL write into the primary checkout, delete a file outside, rename a file outside, rmtree the primary checkout, MOVE-IN the whole checkout, create a junction to the checkout, write through such a junction, hardlink to a file outside, write HKCU registry, spawn a Medium-integrity child, write through an UNBOUNDED inherited handle. ALLOWED write inside the worktree, write %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow, READ the primary checkout, READ the user profile, APPEND to its own Low log.
claims.why: No code in this chunk implements or tests these claims; they refer to measurements not present.

claims.text: NO CAPABILITY CROSSES THE BOUNDARY THAT THE LOW CHILD COULD NOT HAVE OBTAINED ITSELF.
claims.why: Invariant stated but no enforcement code in chunk.

claims.text: EXACTLY ONE handle crosses, selected by name via PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST.
claims.why: No code for PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST in chunk.

claims.text: MEASURED: a deliberately inheritable handle on a Medium file, left off the allowlist, came back ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE (6) in the child and the file was unchanged.
claims.why: Measurement not present in chunk.

claims.text: That handle carries FILE_APPEND_DATA | FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES | SYNCHRONIZE and NOTHING else -- see :data:`WHY_READ_ATTRIBUTES` for the one right the ruling did not name and the measurement that forced it.
claims.why: LOW_APPEND_ACCESS constant matches this mask, and WHY_READ_ATTRIBUTES explains the inclusion.

claims.text: The handle is opened with NtCreateFile rather than CreateFileW because CreateFileW adds rights of its own accord (measured: 0x00100084 handed back when 0x00100004 was requested), and a mask you did not choose cannot be checked as an equality. NtCreateFile grants exactly what is asked.
claims.why: No NtCreateFile or CreateFileW call in chunk.

claims.text: MEASURED IN THE CHILD, with the mask actually shipped: read -> ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (5), SetEndOfFile -> ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (5).
claims.why: Measurement not present.

claims.text: The target must be a LOW-labelled file, and that is checked ON THE OPENED HANDLE, never on the path -- otherwise a reparse point or a swap between check and open reopens the whole bypass. An unlabelled file is implicitly Medium and is REFUSED.
claims.why: No integrity label check code in chunk.

claims.text: The share mode excludes FILE_SHARE_DELETE and FILE_SHARE_WRITE. Without that the child DELETES its own log by path -- measured, the first guarded run destroyed the file -- because a Low-labelled file is fully writable by a Low process, and could then replace it with fabricated gate output. With it: PermissionError.
claims.why: No file open code with share mode in chunk.

claims.text: bInheritHandles=True is written as allowlist is not None. There is no state in which inheritance is on and the allowlist is off, because they are the same expression.
claims.why: No code using allowlist or bInheritHandles in chunk.

claims.text: A handle to a Low-labelled, append-only log does not violate the invariant: a Low child could have opened that file itself. A handle to a Medium file does, and is refused.
claims.why: No handle validation code in chunk.

claims.text: WRITE containment: strong. Eleven distinct write/destroy vectors were tried and refused, including the move-in that no code check can close.
claims.why: No test code in chunk.

claims.text: CONFIDENTIALITY: NONE. MIC is a write-UP barrier. A contained candidate may read the whole checkout and the user profile. Nothing here prevents exfiltration and no caller may read it that way.
claims.why: No mechanism to prevent reading; claim is design statement.

claims.text: NOT a write allowlist. AppData\LocalLow and other Low-labelled objects stay writable. This is damage limitation.
claims.why: No code enforcing allowlist.

claims.text: NETWORK: unrestricted. A Low process still has a network stack, and NO Job Object limit can change that -- see :data:`JOB_LIMITS_DO_NOT_COVER`.
claims.why: JOB_LIMITS_DO_NOT_COVER includes 'network egress: there is no Job Object limit for it.'

claims.text: NAMED PIPES: UNMEASURED. Review declined to call MIC a reliable IPC boundary and so does this module -- see :func:`unmeasured_vectors`, which GREW when bounded inheritance landed and must never shrink silently.
claims.why: UNMEASURED tuple includes 'named pipes: a Medium server with a Low client was not measured'.

claims.text: KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE -- the tree dies with the last handle, so a leaked test process cannot outlive the attempt and keep writing into a worktree that is about to be removed.
claims.why: No job creation code in chunk.

claims.text: ACTIVE_PROCESS -- :data:`JOB_ACTIVE_PROCESS_LIMIT` concurrent processes. Past it CreateProcess IN THE CHILD fails with ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_QUOTA (1816); the job is not killed, so a fork bomb stalls instead of taking the box.
claims.why: No job limit setting code in chunk.

claims.text: JOB_MEMORY -- :data:`JOB_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES` of committed memory across the WHOLE tree, not per process, because per-process caps compose badly with a process cap: N children each just under the line is still N times the line.
claims.why: No job memory limit code in chunk.

claims.text: DIE_ON_UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION -- a crashing candidate dies instead of raising a Windows Error Reporting dialog that no one is there to dismiss, which on an unattended gate is an infinite hang dressed as a slow test.
claims.why: No job creation code in chunk.

claims.text: BREAKAWAY IS DENIED BY OMISSION. Neither BREAKAWAY_OK nor SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK is set, so CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB in the child fails. That is the default, and defaults are exactly what drift, so the read-back below ASSERTS their absence rather than assuming it.
claims.why: No job creation or read-back code in chunk.

claims.text: EVERY ONE OF THOSE IS READ BACK out of the kernel with QueryInformationJobObject and compared before a child is allowed to start. SetInformationJobObject returning TRUE is a claim; LimitFlags coming back out of the kernel is a fact, and only facts reach the attestation.
claims.why: No QueryInformationJobObject code in chunk.

claims.text: Only the GATE CHILD is contained. The harness process that spawns it, the git calls it makes, and attempt.py's _persist all run at the invoking user's full integrity, by construction -- something has to hold the Medium handles.
claims.why: No harness code in chunk.

claims.text: daedalus.primary_tree's fence resolves a path and then writes to it, and a junction swapped in between those two steps is NOT closed by Python; nothing written in Python can close it. MIC containment of the child is the mechanism that actually bounds that class, because the swap only buys the attacker a write the KERNEL will still refuse at Low integrity.
claims.why: No primary_tree code in chunk.

claims.text: An AppContainer or a restricted token with its own SID would bound network, IPC, capabilities and confidentiality. That belongs in its own ADR with its own threat model. This is the first step that is measurably better than nothing.
claims.why: No AppContainer or restricted token code in chunk.

claims.text: LOW_APPEND_ACCESS = (_FILE_APPEND_DATA | _FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES | _SYNCHRONIZE)  # 0x00100084
claims.why: Constant is defined with those values; 0x0004 | 0x0080 | 0x00100000 = 0x00100084.

claims.text: FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES is granted because os.fstat(1) needs it and pytest silently redirects all output to os.devnull when it fails -- measured: exit 0 with zero bytes captured.
claims.why: Measurement not present in chunk.

claims.text: It is a read right on a Low-labelled file the contained child could have opened itself, so no capability crosses that it did not already have.
claims.why: No integrity check code in chunk.

claims.text: JOB_ACTIVE_PROCESS_LIMIT = 96. Concurrent processes allowed inside the gate's job. MEASURED, not guessed: a real contained python -m pytest of this repo's own tests was run with the job's accounting counters read back afterwards, and the number below is that measured peak with a wide margin over it.
claims.why: Measurement not present.

claims.text: JOB_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES = 4 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024. Same reasoning: far above a measured real run, far below 'this box stops responding'.
claims.why: Measurement not present.

claims.text: JOB_LIMITS_DO_NOT_COVER = ("network egress: there is no Job Object limit for it...", "confidentiality: the caps bound consumption, not reads...", "disk: JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_JOB_MEMORY is COMMITTED MEMORY...", "the harness itself: only the gate CHILD is in the job...")
claims.why: Tuple is defined with those strings.

claims.text: UNMEASURED = ("named pipes: a Medium server with a Low client was not measured...", "network egress: a Low process still has a full network stack", "reading: MIC is a write-up barrier and does not restrict reads at all", "log path disclosure: the child can recover the log's full path from the inherited handle via GetFinalPathNameByHandle (measured, it works)...", "the log AFTER the run: once this process closes the inherited handle the share-mode guard is gone...", "handle-value reuse: the allowlist is verified immediately before CreateProcessAsUserW...", "GrantedAccess is the kernel's accounting of OUR handle...")
claims.why: Tuple is defined with those strings.

observations.what: Module docstring contains extensive design documentation but no executable code.
JOB_ACTIVE_PROCESS_LIMIT and JOB_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES are defined but not used in this chunk.
UNMEASURED tuple includes seven entries, but the docstring says 'the three original entries ever disappear'.
WHY_READ_ATTRIBUTES refers to a measurement that is not present in this chunk.
